summary.intent: Add a diagnostic to the callisto release command that warns when a release tag exists locally but not on origin, so half-finished releases are not silently abandoned. This follows the already-opened PR #355.
summary.outcome: Added a graph-level function that finds local-only tags and wired it into the CLI to warn per missing tag before planning. Added an e2e test, a spec criterion and a changeset, ran the full CI pipeline, then committed, pushed and opened a PR.

repo: Work is done in a git worktree at .claude/worktrees/smoke-main; each feature branches from main and gets its own PR.
Release logic is split between callisto-graph (commands/release/local.rs, re-exported through the release module and commands/mod.rs) and callisto-cli (commands/release.rs).
New graph functions must be re-exported through the release module and then commands before the CLI can use them.
The CLI e2e test harness uses a fake git. It maps origin to a local bare repo and keeps the fake remote's tags in a record file, which ls-remote reads.
Release behaviour is documented in docs/specs/release.json as criteria, and changes extend the relevant criterion, such as the rerun one.
Changes require a .changeset/*.md file and a full CI pipeline run, including clippy, which flags unneeded `mut`.

code.finding: To simulate a tag missing from the remote, write the harness's fake-remote tag record file directly. Using real_git_push against the wrong remote did not work.
Holds the new function that compares local tags with the tags the remote reports, using the tag provider's remote query.

workflow: Read the existing handler and helper signatures before writing the new function and wiring.
Run the new e2e test early. It showed the first assertion passed and only the test's push setup was wrong, which narrowed the fix.
When a test harness fakes a tool, inspect how the fake stores state, since writing that state directly can be simpler than driving real commands.
Run formatting and the full CI pipeline before committing.

friction: The first e2e test attempt pushed to the wrong remote because the harness's origin mapping differs from a real bare remote. This took several lookups across other tests to resolve.
A leftover `mut` in the test would have failed clippy and needed a cleanup pass.
